name: Medicine Ball Push-Up Switch
description: A dynamic push-up variation where one hand rests on a medicine ball while the other is on the floor. After each repetition, the ball is rolled to the opposite hand, alternating which arm receives the elevated unstable position. This creates a lateral shifting load pattern that trains unilateral pressing strength, shoulder stability, and anti-rotation core control in an alternating fashion.

execution.starting_position: Begin in a high plank with one hand on a medicine ball and the other on the floor, hands roughly shoulder-width apart in total.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a firm, smooth-surfaced medicine ball that rolls easily on the floor surface. A rubberized floor or smooth tile works best for the rolling transition.
steps: Step 1: Begin with right hand on ball, left hand on floor. Perform one controlled push-up.
Step 2: At the top of the push-up, shift weight to the left hand and roll the ball from the right hand to the left hand.
Step 3: Reestablish balance with left hand on ball, right hand on floor. Perform the next push-up.
Step 4: Roll ball back to the right and repeat. Each push-up on each side counts as one rep.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale on descent, exhale on press. Breathe normally during the ball transfer.
common_mistakes: Rolling the ball before fully completing the push-up
Losing hip alignment during the lateral weight shift
Using a ball that is too large, making the hand-to-floor height difference too great
safety_considerations: Ensure the ball does not roll away rapidly — keep one hand on it at all times
On slippery floors, place ball against a wall to limit travel
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Full push-up range on each side. The ball-side hand gets a greater stretch depth due to elevation.
coaching_cues: Control the ball roll — do not let it get away from you
Keep hips square and level during the lateral transfer
